name: Genetic Renal Tubular Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic Renal Tubular Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with renal tubular function
Evidence of renal tubular dysfunction such as electrolyte imbalances or acid-base disturbances
Positive family history of renal tubular disease or related symptoms
Abnormal urinary excretion of electrolytes or low molecular weight proteins

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of renal tubular dysfunction plus either genetic confirmation or a positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and guide management.

searchTerms: excess salt and minerals in urine

pathognomonic.symptomName: Metabolic acidosis due to proximal or distal tubular dysfunction
searchTerms: acid buildup from kidney tubule problems
blood acidity due to kidney dysfunction
potassium loss due to kidney defects

common.symptomName: Polyuria due to impaired tubular reabsorption
searchTerms: excessive urination from kidney reabsorption problem
too much urine output due to kidney issues

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness related to electrolyte imbalance
searchTerms: weak muscles due to mineral imbalance
muscle fatigue related to electrolyte loss
calcium deposits in kidneys on scan

rare.symptomName: Rickets or osteomalacia secondary to phosphate wasting
searchTerms: bone weakness due to low phosphate

laboratory: Hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, metabolic acidosis or alkalosis depending on tubular segment affected
Elevated urinary excretion of electrolytes (e.g., potassium, phosphate, magnesium)
imaging: Nephrocalcinosis on renal ultrasound or CT scan
genetic: Mutations in genes encoding renal tubular transport proteins (e.g., SLC12A3, CLCN5, SLC34A1)
other: Family history of similar renal tubular disorders

distinguishingFeatures: Hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with hyperreninemia and hyperaldosteronism
Genetic mutations distinct from other tubulopathies
Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction with glucosuria, aminoaciduria, and phosphaturia

redFlags: Severe electrolyte imbalances refractory to supplementation
Progressive renal impairment or chronic kidney disease
Early onset growth failure or developmental delay
references: GeneReviews: Disorders of Renal Tubular Transport
